_comment: Cross-check vectors for the normalization C15 clause 3 compares against.
The function exists TWICE, and it has to. `normalized_source_hash` in patch_side.py runs
outside on the diff; `_normalized` in harness/oracle/fingerprints.py runs INSIDE the
oracle image, where it must, because D54 forbids the oracle's source crossing the
boundary at all -- only digests may cross. And extract.py's stated property is that
nothing baked into that image imports Alfred code, so the two cannot share a module.
Two implementations of a canonical form is the hazard ACS-1 already named and already
solved: publish vectors and make both sides answer them. If the two normalizations ever
disagree, every hash in policy/oracle-source-hashes.json is a hash of something else and
clause 3 silently matches nothing -- which reads exactly like a clean patch.
The vectors are chosen for the rules that differ between plausible implementations, not
for coverage: comment stripping at end of line vs whole line, both comment syntaxes,
whitespace runs across newlines, leading and trailing trim, and case folding.

vectors.name: slash-comment
